note.question: When should a physical fashion retailer adopt AR fitting, and how do congestion, match accuracy, complementarity, technology friction, and price flexibility determine retailer revenue and consumer welfare?
note.overview: A monopoly retailer first chooses whether to adopt in-store AR fitting and then, when prices are adjustable, selects price; heterogeneous time-sensitive consumers strategically choose physical fitting, AR only, sequential AR-plus-fitting, or exit. Their aggregate choices determine congestion and fixed-point queueing equilibrium.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The retailer first chooses whether to adopt AR fitting and then sets price in the adjustable-price scenario; the price is fixed in the luxury-style benchmark. Consumers then choose physical fitting, AR only, AR followed by physical fitting, or exit based on expected utilities and the equilibrium fitting-room wait. Aggregate choices determine congestion, so consumer thresholds and waiting time must be mutually consistent. AR provides an immediate but imperfect path, while the physical fitting room is more accurate but congestible.
